questions.q: State the key conditions required for a random variable to be modeled by a Poisson distribution.
questions.answer: Events occur independently of one another; events occur at a constant average rate over the given interval of time or space; two events cannot occur at exactly the same instant; the number of events in non-overlapping intervals is independent.

questions.q: Explain why the number of texts a person receives in a randomly chosen hour might reasonably be modeled by a Poisson distribution, but the number of texts received right around a pre-arranged deadline might not.
questions.answer: Texts received during a typical hour occur independently and at a roughly constant average rate, satisfying the Poisson conditions. Texts clustered around a pre-arranged deadline (e.g. everyone replying just before a cutoff) violate the constant-rate and independence assumptions, since there is a systematic surge rather than random, uniform occurrence.

questions.q: A shop receives an average of $3$ customers per minute, modeled by $X\sim\text{Po}(3)$. Find $P(X=5)$, to three decimal places.
Using the same shop, find $P(X=1)$, to three decimal places.
Using the same shop, find $P(X\leq2)$.

sections.heading: Mean and variance of a Poisson distribution

questions.q: State the mean and variance of $X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda)$, and find the standard deviation when $\lambda=9$.
questions.answer: $E(X)=\lambda$ and $\text{Var}(X)=\lambda$ — both equal $\lambda$, unlike most other distributions where mean and variance are independent parameters. When $\lambda=9$: standard deviation $=\sqrt{9}=3$.

questions.q: A random variable $X\sim\text{Po}(7)$. State $E(X)$, $\text{Var}(X)$, and the standard deviation, to three decimal places.
Two independent Poisson processes have rates $\lambda_1=4$ and $\lambda_2=6$ per hour. State the distribution of the total number of events, and find its mean and variance.
questions.answer: The sum of independent Poisson variables is itself Poisson: total $\sim\text{Po}(4+6)=\text{Po}(10)$. Mean $=10$; variance $=10$.

questions.q: Three independent Poisson processes have rates $\lambda_1=2$, $\lambda_2=4$, $\lambda_3=5$ per hour. Find the mean and variance of the total number of events across all three processes in one hour.

sections.heading: Poisson as an approximation to the binomial

questions.q: Explain the conditions under which a binomial distribution $X\sim B(n,p)$ can be well-approximated by a Poisson distribution, and state the value of $\lambda$ to use.
questions.answer: The approximation is appropriate when $n$ is large and $p$ is small (a common guideline: $n>50$ and $np<5$), so events are rare relative to the number of trials. Then $X$ is approximately $\text{Po}(\lambda)$ with $\lambda=np$.

questions.q: A factory produces $2000$ items, each independently defective with probability $0.0025$. Using the Poisson approximation, find the probability that exactly $2$ items are defective, to three decimal places.

A survey mails $5000$ questionnaires, each independently containing a printing error with probability $0.0006$. Using the Poisson approximation, find the probability that no questionnaires contain an error, to four decimal places.

A call center receives calls at $\lambda=6$ per 10-minute interval. Find the probability of receiving more than $3$ calls, given $P(X=0)\approx0.00248$, $P(X=1)\approx0.01487$, $P(X=2)\approx0.04462$, $P(X=3)\approx0.08924$.
A website receives visitors at $\lambda=4$ per minute. Find $P(1\leq X\leq3)$, given $P(X=0)\approx0.0183$, $P(X=1)\approx0.0733$, $P(X=2)\approx0.1465$, $P(X=3)\approx0.1954$.
A random variable $X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda)$ satisfies $P(X=0)=0.0498$. Find $\lambda$, to the nearest whole number.
A random variable $X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda)$ has standard deviation $2$. Find $\lambda$, and then find $P(X=\lambda)$, to three decimal places.
A random variable $X\sim\text{Po}(\lambda)$ satisfies $P(X=1)=0.1494$, where $\lambda$ is a whole number less than $5$. Using $P(X=1)=\lambda e^{-\lambda}$, determine $\lambda$ by trial.
questions.answer: Testing $\lambda=3$: $3e^{-3}=3(0.049787)\approx0.1494$ ✓, matching the given probability. So $\lambda=3$.

sections.heading: Poisson processes over different intervals and conditional probability

questions.q: Machine faults occur at an average rate of $\lambda=2$ per day. Find the probability that exactly $2$ faults occur today, given that at least one fault occurs today, to three decimal places, using $P(X=0)\approx0.1353$ and $P(X=2)\approx0.2707$.

A radioactive source emits particles at a rate of $\lambda=1.2$ per second, modeled by a Poisson distribution. Find $P(X=2)$ for a 3-second interval, to three decimal places, using the fact that the parameter scales with the length of the interval.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: quality control at a bottling plant

questions.q: This question has four parts. Faulty caps occur at random in bottling cases with an average rate of $\lambda=1.5$ per case. (a) Find $P(X=0)$ and $P(X=1)$ for a randomly selected case, to four decimal places. (b) Find the probability that a case has at least $2$ faulty caps. (c) The plant inspects $40$ cases per day. Using the fact that a sum of independent Poisson variables is itself Poisson, state the distribution of the total number of faulty caps found across all $40$ cases in a day, and find its mean. (d) Since this total has a large $\lambda$, it can be approximated by $N(\lambda,\lambda)$. Using a continuity correction and $\Phi(1.36)\approx0.9131$, estimate the probability that more than $70$ faulty caps are found in a day.
questions.answer: (a) $P(X=0)=e^{-1.5}\approx0.2231$. $P(X=1)=1.5e^{-1.5}\approx0.3347$. (b) $P(X\geq2)=1-0.2231-0.3347\approx0.4422$. (c) Total $\sim\text{Po}(40\times1.5)=\text{Po}(60)$, with mean $60$. (d) Using $N(60,60)$ with $\sigma=\sqrt{60}\approx7.746$, and a continuity correction for "more than $70$" (i.e. $\geq71$): $z=\dfrac{70.5-60}{7.746}\approx1.36$. $P(\text{total}>70)\approx1-\Phi(1.36)\approx1-0.9131\approx0.087$.
